questions.question: Properly adjusted mirrors on a school bus allow the driver to see how far behind the bus?

options.text: 50 feet
100 feet
200 feet
1,000 feet

questions.explanation: School bus mirrors must be properly adjusted for safe operation. Flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet behind the bus. This equals about four bus lengths.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses. Do not assume cotter keys are present—you must verify this.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: Retracted.
Fully raised.
More worn on the passenger's side than on the driver's side.
Well lit.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a trailer, make sure the landing gear is fully raised with no missing parts. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: During the drive.
Before beginning to drive.
After the drive is completed.

questions.explanation: School bus mirrors must be properly adjusted for safe operation. Always check and adjust each mirror before you start driving.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate does not go back up after a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to check if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.explanation: If a gate fails to go back up after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not try to drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the left. Park your vehicle completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: See passengers.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror in a school bus is used to watch passengers inside the bus.

questions.question: When students get off the bus, they should:

options.text: Stay seated until told to exit.
Stand up and move toward the door while the bus is moving.
Exit and stand next to the bus until it leaves.
Jump down from the top step.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until told to exit.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until the driver tells them to exit. After exiting, they should walk at least 10 feet away from the bus to a place where the driver can see them.

questions.question: If a student drops an item while approaching the bus, the student should:

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick up the object.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Leave the item and walk away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could disappear from the driver's view at a dangerous moment. Students should move away from the bus's danger zones, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must maintain four points of contact with the vehicle.
May turn to face the road before your exit is complete.
Must be facing away from the vehicle.
Must be facing the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in an automatic failure of the skills test.

questions.question: If a student drops an item near a stopped bus, what should they do?

options.text: Run and pick up the item quickly.
Leave the item where it is.
Ask the driver to pick up the item.
Ask another student to pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the item.
questions.explanation: Students should not try to pick up dropped items themselves. They could move out of the driver's view, which is dangerous. Instead, students should move away from the bus, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: What is the overhead inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: Watch students inside the bus.
Look at the outside of the bus.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus helps the driver watch all students inside. It should be adjusted so the driver can see every student, even those sitting right behind the driver's seat.

questions.question: If a tornado is coming and there is no building nearby, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby ditch
To the closest tree
Near a river

questions.explanation: If students must leave the bus during a tornado warning, the driver should take them to a building for shelter. If no building is available, the driver should lead them to a nearby ditch or culvert. They should stay away from areas that flood and keep far enough from the bus so it cannot fall on them if it tips.

questions.question: When backing into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive straight into the alley parking space.
Turn right to face the alley directly.
Pass the alley and stop at a right angle to it.
Pass the alley and stop parallel to it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the alley and stop parallel to it.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, first pass the alley and stop parallel to its outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space, keeping it lined up within the parking area lines.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well you speak.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your overall driving behavior.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and laws, and avoid accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Stop on the tracks.
Change gears.
Try to pass another vehicle.
Stay in your lane.

questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, you must not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: What does ABS help you do?

options.text: Lock up the wheels.
Prevent the wheels from locking up.
Count the students on the bus.
Predict the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located?

options.text: On the outside left of the bus.
On the outside right of the bus.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus.

questions.question: When loading or unloading students, the bus transmission should be placed in:

options.text: Reverse.
Fourth gear.
Neutral.
First gear.

questions.explanation: When the bus is stopped for loading or unloading students, put the transmission in park. If the bus has no park setting, use neutral instead.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.
